items.bold: IRGC: Any vessel approaching Hormuz = targeting. Near-miss with US minesweeper.
items.text: IRGC issued formal statement: "Approaching the Strait of Hormuz will be considered cooperation with the enemy, and any violating vessel will be targeted." The threat is now explicit and unconditional. Separately, Ghalibaf revealed Iran nearly fired on a US Navy minesweeper in the strait — he told the Islamabad delegation "if the minesweeper moved even slightly forward from its position, we would definitely fire at it." US backed down. This shows how close the situation is to kinetic escalation between the two navies. For India: no safe transit of Hormuz until Iran lifts its closure condition — blockade removal.

items.bold: India MEA: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri expressed deep concern over Indian ships.
items.text: India's MEA confirmed Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met with India's ambassador to Iran to express deep concern about the shooting incident involving two Indian-flagged vessels. MEA noted Iran had "facilitated the safe passage of several ships bound for India" — suggesting India was still on Iran's "friendly" list and the IRGC attack may have been uncoordinated with Iran's civilian and diplomatic track. India is working the back channel with Tehran to understand what happened. India-Iran had established a special arrangement (India was among five nations given transit rights in March). That arrangement appears to have broken down with the IRGC reclosure.

items.bold: No date set for second round Islamabad talks — Iran insists on framework first.
items.text: Iran Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh at diplomacy forum in Antalya, Turkey: "There is no set date for the next round of talks between the US and Iran. Until we agree on the framework, we cannot, you know, set the date." This is a significant setback for the weekend timeline Trump suggested Friday. NBC News live blog headline: "NEW TALKS BUT NO TIMELINE: Iranian officials say new US proposals are under review." Iran wants framework agreement before scheduling another round — not another open-ended 21-hour session without result.

items.bold: TRUMP Air Force One: "Maybe I won't extend ceasefire. May have to start bombing again."
items.text: Trump on Air Force One Saturday: "Maybe I won't extend it" (referring to ceasefire). "So you'll have a blockade, and unfortunately we'll have to start dropping bombs again." Then immediately: "I think it's going to happen" (re: a deal). This is maximum pressure language — using threat of resumed strikes alongside diplomatic hope signal. The ceasefire expires April 22. With no second round confirmed and Hormuz reclosed, April 22 expiry without extension would be the most dangerous day since February 28. Iran: "uncertainty is the name of the game" (Al Jazeera Tehran correspondent).

items.bold: Al Jazeera: 8+ ships crossed before reclosure — Indian VLCC among them.
items.text: By 10:30 GMT Saturday, at least 8 oil and gas tankers had crossed the strait in the brief opening window — but at least as many ships turned back (AFP data). The Indian VLCC carrying 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude had been given clearance and was transiting when IRGC gunboats approached without VHF challenge and opened fire. Republic TV has audio of the captain's mayday call. India was among nations Iran labelled "friendly" — China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iraq had special transit arrangements since March. The IRGC attack on Indian ships represents a significant breakdown of those arrangements and Iran's civilian-military coordination failure.

items.bold: Iran's full demands — what a deal actually requires.
items.text: Al Jazeera Tehran correspondent laid out Iran's comprehensive demands: (1) nuclear program framework and HEU stockpile resolution, (2) Hormuz sovereignty recognition, (3) sanctions relief, (4) $6 billion frozen assets unfrozen, (5) Lebanon and regional ceasefire framework, (6) security guarantees against future US/Israeli strikes. "Iran is looking for a comprehensive end to the war across the region," the correspondent said. This explains why Iran insists on framework first before setting a date — one-issue sessions keep collapsing. US position (Rubio): civilian nuclear program OK, weapons-grade enrichment must stop. Gap: 20yr US vs 5yr Iran enrichment pause.

assessment.body:
Day 51 opens with the war at its most dangerous inflection point since February 28.

THE HORMUZ CRISIS — WHERE WE ARE NOW
• Hormuz CLOSED. IRGC: any approaching vessel = target
• IRGC nearly fired on US minesweeper — US Navy backed down
• Brief opening Friday-Saturday: 8+ ships crossed, then IRGC fired on Indian VLCC
• Indian-flagged VLCC (2 million barrels Iraqi crude) attacked DESPITE clearance
• India MEA: Foreign Secretary Misri expressing deep concern via ambassador
• India-Iran back channel: MEA noted Iran had "facilitated safe passage" for India ships
• Suggests civilian-military coordination breakdown in Iran, not deliberate India-targeting
• But IRGC formal policy now: any approaching vessel = enemy cooperation = target

NO DATE FOR ROUND 2 — IRAN INSISTS ON FRAMEWORK FIRST
• Iran Deputy FM Khatibzadeh (Antalya): "Until we agree on framework, we cannot set date"
• US has sent new proposals — Iran reviewing
• Iran's six demands: nuclear, Hormuz, sanctions, $6B assets, Lebanon, security guarantees
• These cannot be resolved in another 21-hour single session
• Rubio's civilian-nuclear concession (April 18) stands — most significant US move of the war
• But Iran needs comprehensive framework, not sequential single-issue talks
